[
  {"step": 1, "file": "src/bin/fuzz/config_fuzzer.cc", "function": "LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput", "line": 53, "var": "static_data", "code": "config = config_open_for_fuzzing(static_data, size);", "note": "Attacker-controlled input (32768 bytes ending with '$') is copied to static_data global buffer and passed to config parser"},
  {"step": 2, "file": "src/lib/lwan-config.c", "function": "config_init_data", "line": 740, "var": "lexer->pos", "code": "lexer = { .pos = data, .start = data, .end = (char *)data + len }", "note": "Lexer initialized with pos=start=static_data, end=static_data+32768 (one past the global array)"},
  {"step": 3, "file": "src/lib/lwan-config.c", "function": "lex_config", "line": 430, "var": "chr", "code": "int chr = next(lexer);", "note": "next() reads each byte of 'aaa...a$' until it reaches '$' at the last position, advancing pos to end"},
  {"step": 4, "file": "src/lib/lwan-config.c", "function": "lex_config", "line": 455, "var": "lexer->pos", "code": "if (chr == '$' && peek(lexer) == '{')", "note": "chr is '$', so peek() is called to check if next char is '{'"},
  {"step": 5, "file": "src/lib/lwan-config.c", "function": "peek", "line": 285, "var": "lexer->pos", "code": "int chr = next(lexer);", "note": "next() sees pos(==end) >= end, sets pos = end+1 (static_data+32769), returns '\\0'"},
  {"step": 6, "file": "src/lib/lwan-config.c", "function": "backup", "line": 278, "var": "lexer->pos", "code": "lexer->pos--;", "note": "backup() decrements pos from end+1 to end (static_data+32768), which is one past the global array"},
  {"step": 7, "file": "src/lib/lwan-config.c", "function": "backup", "line": 279, "var": "*lexer->pos", "code": "if (*lexer->pos == '\\n')", "note": "GLOBAL-BUFFER-OVERFLOW READ: reads *pos where pos == static_data+32768, which is 1 byte past the end of the 32768-byte static_data global array"}
]
EOF

message.content:
Now I have a global-buffer-overflow! The crash is at `backup` called from `peek` called from `lex_string`. The stack trace is slightly different from the OSS-Fuzz report (which says "backup peek lex_config"), but the root cause is the same - the `backup` function reads out of bounds.

Let me update the trace to reflect the exact path with the 32768-byte input:
